options: Kubernetes administration skills only
Designing and implementing DevOps solutions on Microsoft Azure — pipelines, IaC, monitoring

questions.explain: AZ-400 covers source control strategy, CI/CD pipeline design, infrastructure as code, and monitoring on Azure, closely matching the capstone's own architecture.

questions.q: What makes the CKA exam different from the other three certifications covered in this lesson?
options: It is entirely multiple choice
It is a fully hands-on, performance-based exam conducted in a live terminal
It requires no prior Kubernetes experience
It only covers Terraform, not Kubernetes
questions.explain: Unlike AZ-400, AWS DevOps Pro, and Terraform Associate, CKA is performance-based: candidates complete real tasks on live clusters in a terminal rather than answering multiple-choice questions.

questions.q: Why is AWS Certified DevOps Engineer – Professional considered harder to pass 'cold' than AZ-400?
options: It has fewer questions
It is a professional-tier exam assuming real hands-on AWS experience and leans heavily on scenario-based questions
It does not require any DevOps knowledge
It is multiple choice only with no scenarios
questions.explain: As a professional-tier certification, it assumes substantial hands-on AWS experience and emphasizes scenario-based questions over straightforward recall.

questions.q: Why is the Terraform Associate certification described as a good first certification for someone newer to the field?
options: It requires no knowledge of Terraform at all
It is multiple choice, covers core workflow and state concepts, and does not require a live terminal
It is the hardest of the four certifications
It only covers Kubernetes, not Terraform
questions.explain: Terraform Associate is multiple choice and covers core concepts like init/plan/apply/destroy, state, and modules, making it more approachable than CKA's live performance exam.
